problem.text: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 6$, $BC = 7$, and $CA = 8$. Point $D$ lies on $\overline{BC}$, and $\overline{AD}$ bisects $\angle BAC$. Point $E$ lies on $\overline{AC}$, and $\overline{BE}$ bisects $\angle ABC$. The bisectors intersect at $F$. What is the ratio $AF : FD$?

steps.title: Where to start: angle bisectors call for the angle bisector theorem
steps.body: Both segments are angle bisectors, and the angle bisector theorem says a bisector splits the opposite side in the same ratio as the two sides next to the angle. Start with $AD$: it splits $BC = 7$ into $BD$ and $DC$ with $\frac{BD}{DC} = \frac{AB}{AC}$. Careful: $BD$ is the piece next to $B$, so it goes with $AB$.

steps.title: Look inside triangle $ABD$
steps.body: The ratio we want is along $AD$, so find a bisector that cuts $AD$. In triangle $ABD$, the segment $BF$ goes from vertex $B$ to the opposite side $AD$. It is part of $BE$, so it bisects the angle at $B$ of this smaller triangle too. That means the angle bisector theorem applies again, this time in triangle $ABD$.

your_turn.prompt: Why is the angle at $B$ in triangle $ABD$ the same angle as $\angle ABC$?
your_turn.answer: Because $D$ lies on side $BC$, so ray $BD$ is the same as ray $BC$. So $BE$, which bisects $\angle ABC$, also bisects $\angle ABD$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
In triangle $ABD$, bisector $BF$ splits side $AD$ in the ratio of the sides next to $B$:
$$\frac{AF}{FD} = \frac{AB}{BD} = \frac{6}{3} = 2.$$
So $AF : FD = 2 : 1$. (The point $E$ and the lengths on $AC$ are not needed.) The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.A: This comes from pairing the pieces the wrong way in the first step, getting $BD = 4$ instead of $3$; then $\frac{AB}{BD} = \frac64 = \frac32$. Remember the piece of $BC$ next to $B$ goes with the side $AB$ next to $B$.
